what_it_does: When a chip that runs AI neural networks (a DNN accelerator) must be made secure, the standard approach is to encrypt data before writing it to off-chip memory and verify its integrity when reading it back. But this adds hardware cost and slows down the chip because encryption and verification checks require extra time and memory bandwidth. SeDA proposes a set of coordinated hardware and software techniques to reduce these overheads: a bandwidth-aware encryption scheme that avoids wasted memory transfers, a careful choice of how large each encrypted block of data should be (trading off encryption overhead against the number of memory accesses), and a multi-level integrity checking scheme that avoids extra round-trips to memory. The result is a secure accelerator whose performance penalty is much smaller than naive encryption approaches.
